hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with history and global artists
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is reshaping Fort Pierce's cultural landscape by establishing the Peacock Arts District as a hub for artistic expression. Located within the historic Crain Estate, this nonprofit organization honors the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the property's original owners. The estate has been preserved to maintain its historical integrity, with about 90 percent of the space remaining exactly as it was during the Crains' residence, according to art director Krystal Masters.

Jaxson Crain's profession as a tile worker left an indelible mark on the property. His craftsmanship is evident throughout the facility, visible in the flooring, walls, and ceilings. The Crains' extensive world travels, documented in nine separate journeys, resulted in a remarkable collection of global artifacts now displayed at the estate. Among their acquisitions is a gazebo imported from India, which features decorative peacock motifs. The house retains distinctive spaces from the Crains' era, including a smoking and bourbon room with wood paneling, a bathroom decorated in masculine tones, and pre-stained glass leading to a patio bar. Guided tours are offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, allowing visitors to explore the manicured gardens and distinctive architecture.

The foundation takes its name from the peacocks that have inhabited the property for decades. The Crains are credited with introducing peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, beginning with seven birds that have since multiplied to over one hundred. A standout resident is Bob, a peacock believed to be sixty years old and recognizable by his distinctive limp. Bob lives in the house with his own food bowls and receives hand-feeding from tour guides daily. His presence delights young visitors, who often have the opportunity to feed him directly. The Crains' collection extended beyond peacocks; Jackson reportedly traveled to South America, obtained a baby monkey, and transported it home in his pocket.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that welcomes creative professionals from around the world, providing simple yet elegant housing on the grounds. The on-site art lab serves both children and adults through accessible classes and workshops. Krystal leads one-on-one instruction designed for complete beginners, enabling participants to arrive with no experience and leave with finished artwork. The lab offers diverse mediums and projects, including sculpting and watercolor painting. Krystal conducts themed workshops such as "Paint Your Pet in Watercolor and Rainbow." She views art as a therapeutic practice that helps people decompress and disconnect from digital distractions. For Krystal, the most rewarding aspect of her work is watching students leave feeling fulfilled and happy.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor exercised his line-item veto authority to cut nearly $810 million from the spending plan, while blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or maybe nice to have, distancing himself from his 2022 record when he vetoed $3.1 billion in budget funds. The Governor touted the budget as investing billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The new budget also sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades.

Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million to increase correctional officers salaries. The Legislature had added the potential $750 million rainy-day fund transfer to prepare for a new requirement under a proposed constitutional amendment the House passed last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million it labeled budget turkeys.

DeSantis vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations Florida TaxWatch wanted eliminated. The Governor indicated he does not plan to formally lead any political committee to campaign for the proposed amendment after the Legislature changed his proposal, though he did not rule out providing support if asked. The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his term as Governor.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, and South Florida drivers are experiencing the consequences of the surge. AAA estimates that 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million of those trips made by car. This marks an all-time high for the holiday weekend. The heavy rain on Friday added another layer of difficulty to the already congested Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando, creating hazardous driving conditions for travelers.

The wet weather tested drivers' abilities on the crowded roadways. "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive," driver Ed Budd said about Friday's conditions. Despite the challenging circumstances, most drivers continued their journeys. Jim Macfawn acknowledged the difficulties but maintained a positive attitude, saying "I have a lot of experience driving, so I just roll with the punches." Macfawn also noted the sheer scale of travel this year, remarking "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

Orlando and Miami are among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. However, driver experiences varied significantly. Carlos Borras and his wife traveled between Orlando and Miami on Friday and had a smooth trip. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras reported. In contrast, another driver, Fernando Amado, encountered very different conditions. "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather," Amado said. "I thought people were leaving yesterday, but today is the day when people are really heading up North."

For travelers still planning to hit the road, AAA recommends strategic timing to avoid the worst congestion. Those heading out should leave after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. Where travelers are coming from, where they are headed, and what time they leave all impact their experience on the road. With record numbers of Americans traveling and unpredictable weather conditions, careful planning can help make the holiday weekend safer and less stressful for Florida drivers.

cards.headline: Lightning strike kills one person, injures three at Florida beach ahead of holiday weekend
cards.teaser: A lightning strike at a Florida beach left one person dead and three others injured ahead of the July Fourth weekend.
cards.body:
A lightning strike at a Florida beach killed one person and injured three others ahead of the Independence Day holiday weekend. The incident occurred as beachgoers gathered for Fourth of July celebrations across the state.

Florida is known as the lightning capital of the United States, with the state experiencing more lightning strikes than any other state. The fatality and injuries serve as a reminder of the dangers posed by summer thunderstorms, which are common in Florida during the holiday season. Authorities continue to urge beachgoers to seek shelter indoors when thunderstorms approach coastal areas.

cards.teaser: A man was fatally shot during a parking dispute at a South Florida Walmart.

A man died after being shot during a parking dispute at a South Florida Walmart. The fatal shooting occurred in the store's parking area.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach is celebrating after being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida community selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of only 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the award to a long-term effort to revitalize the city and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic participation programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award "brings back community pride" and reflects the city's positive momentum. City leaders said the designation celebrates the city's progress and positions the community for future opportunities and continued growth.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as Fourth of July boaters take to the water
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is preparing for hundreds of boaters on the water this Fourth of July weekend with two boats equipped with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are hitting Florida's waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting the Martin County Maritime Response Unit to prepare extra safety measures. Lt. Brett Harry said his team will have two boats with medics stationed in both the north and south areas of Martin County to assist boaters. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Boaters launching from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday, including Brendan and Ashley Shannon with their young daughter and puppy, said safety is their priority on the water. Harry encouraged all boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents seek fence restoration at JB-7 beach access as town considers $6,000 fix
cards.teaser: A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point in Juno Beach is creating tension between Colony Condos residents and summer beachgoers. The town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons, and now residents say people are cutting through their private property.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer with cars parking randomly and people pushing back bushes to cut through with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said confrontations with trespassers have become recurring, and residents now call police instead of confronting people directly after receiving rude responses when telling trespassers the property is private.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, proposing the town could help with a lower-cost fence or a combination of split rail and shrubs. Hill said residents hope the town will reinstall the fence to restore their landscaping and private parking. Beachgoer Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a public lot a couple of blocks away, said he has not witnessed the problems residents describe and has never noticed anyone crossing the fence or shrubs. The council agreed to take up the fence question during its budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiancee Misty Dawn White in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is receiving community support after losing his fiancee, Misty Dawn White, 46, in a deadly home fire Monday. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside their home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke about the loss. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. The timing adds another layer of heartbreak, as Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July and she passed just a few days before her birthday. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem Blue Cross denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, a 48-year-old breast cancer patient, and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving GalaFlex surgical mesh is considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product gives her patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem responded that it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with treatment standards, but without FDA approval for breast reconstruction, the mesh does not meet their coverage standards. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial, and a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for social media comments about conservative a.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, with the timing of a final decision remaining unclear.

cards.teaser: A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, and a fix could cost the town thousands of dollars.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer. Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there. Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day, Hill said.

Hill said residents remember when the fence made the boundary clear. Since it came down, confrontations with trespassers have become a recurring problem. We used to confront them and tell them this is private property, and they would get pretty rude. So, now what we've just been doing is just calling the police, and they've been coming up and confronting them, Hill said. The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence.

Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring. I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs, Halpern said. hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year as inflation hits holiday meals
hero.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
The cost of celebrating Independence Day with a cookout has increased significantly this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, hosting a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from the previous year. The rise reflects broader inflationary pressures affecting grocery prices across multiple food categories that are staples of Fourth of July celebrations.

Inflation is the primary driver behind the higher cookout costs. Ground beef, a centerpiece of many holiday grills, has increased by 5.5%. Hot dog and hamburger buns have risen even more steeply at 7.7%. Strawberries have experienced the sharpest price jump at 12.4%, largely due to damage from a Florida frost that impacted the crop. Ice cream, another popular dessert choice for summer cookouts, has gone up 5.3%. These increases across multiple items have combined to push overall holiday meal expenses higher than they were a year ago.

However, not all food prices have climbed. Shoppers looking to keep their budgets in check will find some relief in the produce aisle. Potato prices have actually decreased this year, offering savings for those planning to serve potato chips or potato salad at their gatherings. Corn prices have been more volatile, though locally grown corn from the Glades region can provide better pricing options for budget-conscious consumers. These lower-priced alternatives can help offset some of the increases seen in other categories.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies for managing cookout expenses during inflationary times. She emphasizes the importance of shopping strategically by comparing prices across different stores to identify the best deals for items on your shopping list. Beyond comparing stores, Woroch highlights that reducing food waste is crucial for families trying to control costs, and this process should begin with creating a detailed meal plan before shopping. By planning meals in advance and being intentional about purchases, families can celebrate the Fourth of July without breaking the bank despite the year-over-year price increases.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves ahead with Midway Road widening and new Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a new partial interchange for Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city. According to Samples, the interchange is designed to accommodate the growth that has already occurred and the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding the partial interchange, which remains in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated system connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway above existing roads. The company estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. According to Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger, the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops. The elevated guideway would resemble a narrow pedestrian bridge, with stations potentially integrated into buildings to shield riders from weather.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing. Glydways currently operates a testing facility in California and has a project under construction near Atlanta's airport expected to begin rides by year's end.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Peacock House Art Foundation connects local and international artists
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain while hosting an artist-in-residency program that attracts creators from around the world.
cards.body:
Tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, the Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by connecting local and international artists. The nonprofit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once lived on the property. Mr. Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character, keeping it approximately 90 percent the way it was when the Crains lived there. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, starting with seven birds that have grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and known for walking with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program offers simple but elegant accommodations for artists from around the world. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with art director Krystal Masters leading one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners, featuring mediums including sculpting and watercolor.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life, and noted they were grateful the call ended safely and proud of the swift response by their Marine Unit deputies.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation that will nearly double slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock closes July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to last one year.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section for boarding, according to Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for the company. Kuyrkendall said the dock plays a central role in the city's identity and economy, noting that on weekends it can get hectic trying to find spots. He said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and for businesses.

hero.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate Spectrum Academy teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
hero.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge arguing a judge erred in recommending reinstatement of Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009.
hero.body:
Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, was suspended last year following social media comments that labeled Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the Martin County School Board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In her order issued last month, Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby for Fourth of July weekend boating rush
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit expects hundreds of boaters on the water this holiday weekend and has two boats with medics on standby in the north and south.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said the team is preparing for hundreds of boaters celebrating the Fourth of July weekend on the water. The unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south areas of Martin County. Harry said the team is ready to help with everything from stubbed toes to cardiac events, potential spinal injuries or other emergencies.

Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from the ramps at Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, saying safety is top of mind. Harry said he wants boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices.

Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The renovation includes a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades will prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section so customers can board there during construction. cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance Misty Dawn White in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire destroyed the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. "It's completely a state of devastation," Fenn said of the home. Fenn remembered White as a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants, played the piano, and was always willing to help others. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday was July 4, just a few days after her death.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic engagement programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award reflects years of work strengthening trust between residents and local government. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to Florida Turnpike near Orlando
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million making the trip by car.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with 72.2 million estimated to travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, according to AAA. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Friday's wet weather created challenging conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said the conditions made for difficulties once the rain started. Driver Jim Macfawn noted the scale of travel this year, remarking on the high gas costs associated with the record number of travelers.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Experiences on the road varied widely for drivers. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported no traffic, no accidents, and a smooth experience. Driver Fernando Amado described busier conditions, particularly due to the weather. AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football sets sights on state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for a state title run in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. A second-round playoff exit left the team believing more was achievable. Head coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the experience of his senior class, noting that most are four-year players who started at the middle school level. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To reach the next level, the Scots are scheduling significantly tougher opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained the strategy: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." For the team, playoff advancement matters most. Senior Jack Whelche stressed that regular season success is secondary. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said summer workouts are driving the team forward.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to help visitors learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages, and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida state parks offer free admission through Sunday for America's 250th anniversary
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is waiving admission fees at state parks from Friday through Sunday to celebrate Independence Day and the nation's semiquincentennial.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection announced it is waiving admission fees at Florida State Parks from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. All residents and visitors can explore the state's award-winning parks at no charge for day use. Florida's state park system offers hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding, as well as historic sites including forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and other landmarks. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and their family to the state parks to enjoy the outdoors, make new memories and support treasured public lands. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award.

Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. Three parks are excluded from the free admission: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. Free admission applies to day use only. All other fees, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals, remain in effect.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining state spending. The term-limited Governor exercised his line-item veto authority to cut nearly $810 million from the spending plan, while blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or maybe nice to have, distancing himself from his 2022 record when he vetoed $3.1 billion in budget funds. The Governor touted the budget as investing billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The new budget also sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades.

Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million to increase correctional officers salaries. The Legislature had added the potential $750 million rainy-day fund transfer to prepare for a new requirement under a proposed constitutional amendment the House passed last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund. Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million it labeled budget turkeys.

DeSantis vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations Florida TaxWatch wanted eliminated. The Governor indicated he does not plan to formally lead any political committee to campaign for the proposed amendment after the Legislature changed his proposal, though he did not rule out providing support if asked. The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his term as Governor.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities celebrate America's 250th with fireworks and parades
cards.teaser: Cities across Southwest Florida are hosting fireworks displays, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations this weekend to mark the nation's semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Communities across Southwest Florida are marking America's 250th birthday with fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations this Independence Day weekend. Festivities are planned from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach.

Bradenton and Palmetto will celebrate together with activities on both sides of the Manatee River, including events along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park will feature 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a kids zone and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the river. Sarasota's bayfront will host its America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m. Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., with fireworks launching at dusk. The display is funded entirely by local residents, businesses and community supporters. Fort Myers will celebrate with a free concert by Deb The Dynamics and a fireworks and drone show at the Caloosa Sound Amphitheater from 7 to 9:30 p.m. Fort Myers Beach will kick off its celebration with a parade starting at 10 a.m. at Bay Oaks Recreation Center, followed by fireworks launched from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m.

cards.headline: Delray Beach opens 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule as part of America250 celebration
cards.teaser: Delray Beach will crack open a time capsule from the nation's 200th birthday during its Fourth of July celebration, an official America250 partner event expected to draw 20,000 people.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition for more than 50 years that draws upward of 20,000 people, is an official America250 partner event on the national calendar. The city will open a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule on the Main Stage at A1A, a half-century message from Americans who celebrated the nation's 200th birthday to those marking its 250th. At 6 p.m., a 60-foot flag will rise at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society.

Beach activities begin at 8 a.m. with the 4's on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest, the city's sand-sculpting showdown presented by local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs. Judging takes place at 11 a.m., with a rule to keep creations patriotic, not political. Guided snorkel and scuba tours explore the S.S. Inchulva, the British steamship that a 1903 hurricane destroyed 150 yards offshore, known today as the Delray Wreck. Evening entertainment includes tribute act Let's Groove Tonight channeling Earth, Wind Fire and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with Digital Vibez performing on the East Road Stage from 6:30 to 9 p.m. A Zambelli fireworks display lights up the Atlantic at 9 p.m.

cards.headline: Marion County stages four synchronized fireworks displays for semiquincentennial
cards.teaser: Marion County will hold simultaneous fireworks shows at four sites across the region as part of Marion Celebrates 250, with activities starting at 5 p.m. and displays at 9 p.m.
cards.body:
Marion County will stage four synchronized fireworks displays under the Marion Celebrates 250 banner to commemorate the semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Each site opens at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks light up the sky at 9 p.m. The locations are Veterans Memorial Park (2601 E. Fort King St., Ocala), Wrigley Fields (405 E. Highway 316, Citra), Dunnellon High School (10055 SW 180th Ave. Rd., Dunnellon) and the Belleview Sportsplex (6501 SE 107th St., Belleview).

The city of Ocala hosts Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration with live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties and activities. The Patriot Parade kicks off at Southeast 16th Avenue, heads up Silver Springs Boulevard and wraps near Southeast 25th Avenue in the early evening, featuring veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations.

Florida is known as the lightning capital of the United States, with the state experiencing more lightning strikes than any other state. The fatality and injuries serve as a reminder of the dangers posed by summer thunderstorms, which are common in Florida during the holiday season. Authorities continue to urge beachgoers to seek shelter indoors when thunderstorms approach coastal areas.

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
hero.body:
A record number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, and South Florida drivers are experiencing the consequences of the surge. AAA estimates that 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million of those trips made by car. This marks an all-time high for the holiday weekend. The heavy rain on Friday added another layer of difficulty to the already congested Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando, creating hazardous driving conditions for travelers.

The wet weather tested drivers' abilities on the crowded roadways. "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive," driver Ed Budd said about Friday's conditions. Despite the challenging circumstances, most drivers continued their journeys. Jim Macfawn acknowledged the difficulties but maintained a positive attitude, saying "I have a lot of experience driving, so I just roll with the punches." Macfawn also noted the sheer scale of travel this year, remarking "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

Orlando and Miami are among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. However, driver experiences varied significantly. Carlos Borras and his wife traveled between Orlando and Miami on Friday and had a smooth trip. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras reported. In contrast, another driver, Fernando Amado, encountered very different conditions. "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather," Amado said. "I thought people were leaving yesterday, but today is the day when people are really heading up North."

For travelers still planning to hit the road, AAA recommends strategic timing to avoid the worst congestion. Those heading out should leave after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. Where travelers are coming from, where they are headed, and what time they leave all impact their experience on the road. With record numbers of Americans traveling and unpredictable weather conditions, careful planning can help make the holiday weekend safer and less stressful for Florida drivers.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with history and global artists
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is reshaping Fort Pierce's cultural landscape by establishing the Peacock Arts District as a hub for artistic expression. Located within the historic Crain Estate, this nonprofit organization honors the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the property's original owners. The estate has been preserved to maintain its historical integrity, with about 90 percent of the space remaining exactly as it was during the Crains' residence, according to art director Krystal Masters.

Jaxson Crain's profession as a tile worker left an indelible mark on the property. His craftsmanship is evident throughout the facility, visible in the flooring, walls, and ceilings. The Crains' extensive world travels, documented in nine separate journeys, resulted in a remarkable collection of global artifacts now displayed at the estate. Among their acquisitions is a gazebo imported from India, which features decorative peacock motifs. The house retains distinctive spaces from the Crains' era, including a smoking and bourbon room with wood paneling, a bathroom decorated in masculine tones, and pre-stained glass leading to a patio bar. Guided tours are offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, allowing visitors to explore the manicured gardens and distinctive architecture.

The foundation takes its name from the peacocks that have inhabited the property for decades. The Crains are credited with introducing peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, beginning with seven birds that have since multiplied to over one hundred. A standout resident is Bob, a peacock believed to be sixty years old and recognizable by his distinctive limp. Bob lives in the house with his own food bowls and receives hand-feeding from tour guides daily. His presence delights young visitors, who often have the opportunity to feed him directly. The Crains' collection extended beyond peacocks; Jackson reportedly traveled to South America, obtained a baby monkey, and transported it home in his pocket.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that welcomes creative professionals from around the world, providing simple yet elegant housing on the grounds. The on-site art lab serves both children and adults through accessible classes and workshops. Krystal leads one-on-one instruction designed for complete beginners, enabling participants to arrive with no experience and leave with finished artwork. The lab offers diverse mediums and projects, including sculpting and watercolor painting. Krystal conducts themed workshops such as "Paint Your Pet in Watercolor and Rainbow." She views art as a therapeutic practice that helps people decompress and disconnect from digital distractions. For Krystal, the most rewarding aspect of her work is watching students leave feeling fulfilled and happy.

"Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive," driver Ed Budd said about his experience. However, not all drivers reported struggling with the conditions. Jim Macfawn, who described himself as having extensive driving experience, said he approaches such challenges by rolling with the punches. Some drivers noted the sheer scale of this year's travel numbers. Macfawn expressed surprise at the volume, saying "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

Experiences on the road differed significantly depending on when and where drivers traveled. Carlos Borras and his wife completed a round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday without incident. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras said. In contrast, driver Fernando Amado described heavier conditions, noting that Friday was actually when people were really heading north despite expectations that they would have left the day before. "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather," Amado said.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. The timing of departure significantly impacts the driving experience. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. Where drivers are coming from, where they are going, and when they choose to leave can all influence their experience on the road.

cards.headline: Sebastian hosts watermelon eating contest for July 4th celebration
cards.teaser: Sebastian residents competed in a watermelon eating contest on Independence Day as part of the city's Fourth of July festivities.
cards.body:
Sebastian held a watermelon eating contest on Saturday, July 4 as part of the city's Independence Day celebration. The event provided a traditional way for residents to mark the holiday.

The contest took place on the Fourth of July. The watermelon competition offered participants a way to cool off during the summer holiday weekend.

Sebastian's watermelon eating contest joined other community events across the Treasure Coast marking Independence Day.

cards.headline: Vero Beach buries community time capsule to be opened in 2076
cards.teaser: Vero Beach has buried a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed until 2076.
cards.body:
Vero Beach has buried a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed until 2076. The capsule was interred on Friday, July 3.

The time capsule represents contributions from across the Vero Beach community. It will remain buried for 50 years before being opened during the nation's tricentennial celebration.

The burial marks a milestone for Vero Beach residents who participated in the project. The capsule will provide future generations with a snapshot of life in the community in 2026.

The time capsule is scheduled to be opened in 2076, when residents will have the opportunity to view items and documents placed inside by their predecessors.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition comes with a higher price tag this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have risen in price. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically to manage costs. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list," Woroch said. She added that cutting down food waste is crucial for families, and that begins with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach demonstrated one of the district's biggest success stories, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school for 15 years following five years as assistant principal, attributed the turnaround to curriculum modifications starting three years ago, particularly in the early childhood program for students beginning at age 3. Spady was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: FSU Baseball earns commitment from FGCU pitcher Sebastian Lippman
cards.teaser: Florida State University's baseball program has received a commitment from Florida Gulf Coast University right-handed pitcher Sebastian Lippman.
cards.body:
The Florida State Seminoles baseball program earned a commitment from FGCU right-handed pitcher Sebastian Lippman on Saturday. The announcement was made on July 4.

Lippman pitched for Florida Gulf Coast University before committing to transfer to FSU. The Seminoles continue to build their roster for the upcoming season.

The commitment adds pitching depth to the Florida State baseball program as the team prepares for its next season.

cards.headline: Former Red Wing Sebastian Cossa ready for new opportunity with Mammoth
cards.teaser: Former Detroit Red Wings prospect Sebastian Cossa is preparing for a new chance with the Mammoth organization.
cards.body:
Former Detroit Red Wings goaltender Sebastian Cossa is ready for a new opportunity with the Mammoth. Cossa described the chance as super exciting as he prepares for the next phase of his hockey career.

Cossa previously played in the Red Wings organization before making the move. The goaltender is looking forward to the big chance with his new team.

The Mammoth are adding Cossa to their roster as they prepare for the upcoming season.
